source.title: Some Open Questions in Analysis for Dirichlet Series

accepted.question_text: Let H^p denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series obtained as the closure of Dirichlet polynomials F(s)=sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s} in the norm ||F||_{H^p}=(lim_{T→∞}(1/(2T))∫_{-T}^T |F(it)|^p dt)^{1/p}. Is there a universal constant C, depending only on p and the fixed segment length but not on the polynomial, such that for every Dirichlet polynomial sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}, its L^p integral over any fixed-length segment of the vertical line Re s = 1/2 is at most C times its H^p norm to the p-th power?
accepted.context_brief: embedding problem for H^p Dirichlet series

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 (The embedding problem). Is the Lp integral of a Dirichlet polynomial PN n=1 ann−s over any segment of fixed length on the vertical line Re s = 1/2 bounded by a universal constant times kPN n=1 ann−skpHp ?

accepted.question_text: For 0 < p < 2, characterize the Carleson measures for the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series on the half-plane {Re s > 1/2}.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Characterize Carleson measures for Hp on {Re s > 1/2} for p < 2.

accepted.question_text: If 0 < p < 2 and F belongs to the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series, must the zero set of F in the half-plane Re s > 1/2 satisfy the Blaschke condition there?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Do the zero sets of functions in Hp for p < 2 satisfy the Blaschke condition in the half-plane Re s > 1/2?

accepted.question_text: If 0 < p < 2 and F belongs to the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series, is F locally in the Nevanlinna class?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Are elements of Hp for p < 2 locally in the Nevanlinna class?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p < infinity with p not equal to 2, does the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series admit an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Does Hp have an unconditional basis if p ∈ (1,∞) and p 6= 2?

accepted.question_text: Does the Hardy space H^1 of Dirichlet series have a basis, and does it have an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6. Does H1 have a basis? Does it have an unconditional basis?

accepted.question_text: Consider the Hardy spaces H^p(T^∞) on the infinite-dimensional torus T^∞, viewed as boundary-value spaces for analytic functions on the infinite polydisc D^∞. Give general conditions on a radial or non-tangential approach to the distinguished boundary T^∞ under which Fatou's theorem holds for functions in H^p(T^∞).

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7. Give general conditions for a radial (or non-tangential) approach in D∞ to T∞ such that Fatou’s theorem holds for elements in Hp(T∞).

accepted.question_text: For 0 < p < 1, describe the dual spaces of the Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. Describe the dual spaces of Hp.

accepted.question_text: On the infinite-dimensional torus T^∞, what statement should replace Nehari's theorem for Hankel forms? In particular, what can be said about the Riesz projection acting on L^∞(T^∞) and on other BMO-type spaces on T^∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. What is the counterpart to Nehari’s theorem on T∞? In particular, what can be said about the Riesz projection of L∞(T∞) and other BMO-type spaces on T∞?

accepted.question_text: Let ϕ0(s)=1+sum_{n=2}^∞ (log n)^{-1} n^{-1/2-s}, the analytic symbol associated with the multiplicative Hilbert matrix. Is ϕ0 the Riesz projection of some function in L^∞(T^∞)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Is the symbol ϕ0(s) = 1+ P∞ n=2 (logn)−1n−1/2−s the Riesz projection of a function in L∞(T∞)?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the compact composition operators on the Hilbert Hardy space H^2 of Dirichlet series.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Characterize the compact composition operators on H2.

accepted.question_text: Let F_N(s)=sum_{n=1}^N n^{-s}. Is its H^1 norm little-o of sqrt(N) as N tends to infinity; equivalently, is ||F_N||_{H^1}=o(sqrt(N))?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (Helson’s problem [52]). Is it true that kPN n=1 n−skH1 = o(pN) when N → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer k > 1. For which functions m=m(N) are the L^{2k} norms of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials of length N comparable to their L^2 norms?
accepted.context_brief: higher moments of homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Assume k is an integer larger than 1. For which m (depending on N) will the L2k norms of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials of length N be comparable to their L2 norms?

accepted.question_text: Determine the asymptotic behavior, as N tends to infinity, of the H^p norm of the Dirichlet polynomial sum_{n=1}^N n^{-1/2-s} for 0 < p ≤ 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. Determine the asymptotic behavior of ||PN n=1 n−1/2−s||Hp when N → ∞ for 0 < p ≤ 1.

accepted.question_text: For real parameter γ and 0 < p ≤ 1, determine the precise asymptotic growth as N tends to infinity of the H^p norm of the weighted Dirichlet polynomial sum_{n=1}^N [d(n)]^γ n^{-1/2-s}, where d(n) is the divisor function.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Determine the precise asymptotic growth of kPN n=1 [d(n)]γn−1/2−skHp when N → ∞ for p ≤ 1.

accepted.question_text: Let S_N be the partial sum operator on Dirichlet series given by S_N(sum_{n=1}^∞ a_n n^{-s})=sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}. Determine the precise asymptotic growth, as N tends to infinity, of the operator norm of S_N on H^1; more generally, determine it for H^p when p ≤ 1 and for p = infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5. Determine the precise asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator SN : P∞ n=1 ann−s 7→ PN n=1 ann−s when N → ∞ for p = 1 (or more generally, for p ≤ 1 or p = ∞).

accepted.question_text: Let χ be a random completely multiplicative character obtained by choosing the values χ(p) independently and uniformly on the unit circle for each prime p and then extending multiplicatively to all positive integers n. Determine the almost sure growth rate, as N tends to infinity, of the random character sum sum_{n=1}^N χ(n).

evidence.quote: Problem 4.6. Determine the almost sure growth rate (in N) of the character sum X N n=1 χ(n).

accepted.question_text: Relate the recent estimates for GCD sums sum_{k,ℓ=1}^N (gcd(n_k,n_ℓ))^{2α}/(n_k n_ℓ)^α to the function theory and operator theory of Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1. Link the estimates for GCD sums to the function and operator theory of the spaces Hp.

accepted.question_text: Develop further applications of GCD-sum estimates to the Riemann zeta function, and further conceptual links between those estimates and the zeta function.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Develop further applications to and links with the Riemann zeta function.

accepted.question_text: Let ω be uniformly distributed on [0,T]. Is it true that, as T tends to infinity, max_{h in [0,1]} log|ζ(1/2 + i h + i ω)| = log log T - (3/4) log log log T + E, where the error term E stays bounded in probability?
accepted.context_brief: maximum of shifted zeta on short interval

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. [39] Consider [0,T ] as a probability space, with normalised Lebesgue measure, and denote the corresponding variable by ω ∈ [0,T ]. Then, as T → ∞, one has max h∈[0,1] log|ζ(1/2+ih +iω)| = loglogT − 3/4 logloglogT +E, where the error term E is bounded in probability as T → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Let X(x)=sum_p p^{-1/2}(cos(x log p) cos θ_p + sin(x log p) sin θ_p), where the θ_p are independent random variables uniformly distributed on [0,2π] and p runs over the primes. Study the properties of the associated non-Gaussian chaos exp(β X(x)).
accepted.context_brief: non-Gaussian chaos from random Dirichlet field

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2. [39] Let the field X be defined as in (8). Study the properties non-Gaussian chaos "exp(βX(x))".
